rendered:
1. Aging (activation of the superelastic/shape-memory property), done before coating: the NiTi wires were aged at 600 °C for 1 h under vacuum[1] in a Lindberg Blue quartz CVD tube furnace, then mechanically polished and cleaned.
2. Atomic layer deposition of the vanadium oxide coating: the process ran at a reaction temperature of 200 °C[2] throughout. The document gives no separate duration for this deposition temperature; the coating was built up by repeated ALD cycles.
3. Post-deposition annealing of the coated wires: annealed at 450 °C for 30 min[3] in a Lindberg Blue quartz CVD tube furnace open to air, to achieve crystalline V2O5 coatings.
The preheating of the precursor and oxidizer manifolds is a reagent-handling step, not a treatment of the wire, and is not counted here.
